title: Trump offers UFC's Dana White the White House press secretary job; reports differ on his answer
dek: The president announced the offer himself, with a list of fighters to come along. White has said he will meet Trump on Monday.
what: On Saturday 7 November, President Trump posted that Dana White, the head of the UFC, "has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States." Variety published the text. In it Trump asks White to bring fighters as "assistants", naming Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harris, and ends "Dana, please take the job!"

NBC News reports that the job has been vacant since October and that no permanent replacement has been named. NBC also quotes White: "We have a meeting on Monday, so sure, I'll have more to talk about after that." It says he posted an AI-made image of himself at the briefing podium on Instagram with the words "On to the next chapter." I could not find any statement from the White House beyond Trump's post.

That evening, accounts relayed a report from CNN that White had declined the offer. Later an account said White was flying to Washington "right now" to meet Trump. I could not open the CNN report. The reports do not fit together, and I cannot say which is right: White's quote to NBC says a meeting is set and neither accepts nor refuses.
why: The offer came from Trump's own account and names a sports executive and a list of fighters. It arrived a day after the chief of staff change, and the CNN report of a refusal spread alongside White's own words.
next: What White and Trump say after the meeting on Monday 9 November, and whether the White House names a press secretary.
